requirements.quote:
The lower-order four bits of the Attribute Flags octet are
         unused.  They MUST be zero when sent and MUST be ignored when
         received.
requirements.condition: When sending an Attribute Flags octet
requirements.required_behavior: MUST set the lower-order four bits to zero
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized flags can be masked to check their low four bits.

requirements.quote:
The lower-order four bits of the Attribute Flags octet are
         unused.  They MUST be zero when sent and MUST be ignored when
         received.
requirements.condition: When receiving an Attribute Flags octet
requirements.required_behavior: MUST ignore the lower-order four bits
requirements.why_checkable: Changing only the low four bits must not change attribute handling.

requirements.quote:
The Attribute Type Code octet contains the Attribute Type Code.
         Currently defined Attribute Type Codes are discussed in Section
         5.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Attribute Type Code in the Attribute Type Code octet
requirements.why_checkable: Attribute code placement is directly inspectable.

requirements.quote:
If the Extended Length bit of the Attribute Flags octet is set
         to 0, the third octet of the Path Attribute contains the length
         of the attribute data in octets.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the attribute data length in octets in the third octet of the Path Attribute
requirements.why_checkable: The short length field position, width, and interpretation are inspectable.

requirements.quote:
If the Extended Length bit of the Attribute Flags octet is set
         to 1, the third and fourth octets of the path attribute contain
         the length of the attribute data in octets.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the attribute data length in octets in the third and fourth octets of the Path Attribute
requirements.why_checkable: The extended length field position, width, and interpretation are inspectable.

requirements.quote:
The remaining octets of the Path Attribute represent the
         attribute value and are interpreted according to the Attribute
         Flags and the Attribute Type Code.  The supported Attribute
         Type Codes, and their attribute values and uses are as follows:
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the remaining octets as the attribute value according to Attribute Flags and Attribute Type Code
requirements.why_checkable: The parser dispatch and payload boundaries can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
ORIGIN is a well-known mandatory attribute that defines the
            origin of the path information.  The data octet can assume
            the following values:

               Value      Meaning

               0         IGP - Network Layer Reachability Information
                            is interior to the originating AS

               1         EGP - Network Layer Reachability Information
                            learned via the EGP protocol [RFC904]

               2         INCOMPLETE - Network Layer Reachability
                            Information learned by some other means
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the defined ORIGIN values 0, 1, and 2
requirements.why_checkable: The ORIGIN enumeration can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
0         IGP - Network Layer Reachability Information
                            is interior to the originating AS
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret 0 as IGP: NLRI is interior to the originating AS
requirements.why_checkable: ORIGIN value-to-meaning dispatch is checkable.

requirements.quote:
1         EGP - Network Layer Reachability Information
                            learned via the EGP protocol [RFC904]
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret 1 as EGP: NLRI was learned via the EGP protocol
requirements.why_checkable: ORIGIN value-to-meaning dispatch is checkable.

requirements.quote:
2         INCOMPLETE - Network Layer Reachability

requirements.quote:
This variable length field contains a list of IP address
         prefixes.  The length, in octets, of the Network Layer
         Reachability Information is not encoded explicitly, but can be
         calculated as:
requirements.condition: Encoding or decoding the NLRI field
requirements.required_behavior: Represent NLRI as a variable-length list of IP address prefixes
requirements.why_checkable: The NLRI list representation is inspectable.

requirements.quote:
This variable length field contains a list of IP address
         prefixes.  The length, in octets, of the Network Layer
         Reachability Information is not encoded explicitly, but can be
         calculated as:

               UPDATE message Length - 23 - Total Path Attributes Length
               - Withdrawn Routes Length

         where UPDATE message Length is the value encoded in the fixed-
         size BGP header, Total Path Attribute Length, and Withdrawn
         Routes Length are the values encoded in the variable part of
         the UPDATE message, and 23 is a combined length of the fixed-
         size BGP header, the Total Path Attribute Length field, and the
         Withdrawn Routes Length field.
requirements.condition: Determining the NLRI field length in octets
requirements.required_behavior: Calculate NLRI length as the UPDATE message Length from the fixed BGP header minus 23 minus Total Path Attributes Length minus Withdrawn Routes Length, with the latter lengths taken from the UPDATE variable part
requirements.why_checkable: The payload boundary calculation and its input fields can be checked.

requirements.quote:
